“Seek ye the LORD while He may be found, call ye upon Him while He is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and He will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for He will abundantly pardon.” — Isaiah 55:6-7 (KJV) No matter who you are or where you are in the world, this message has crossed your path today. Perhaps God is using these very words to reach your heart. Jesus Christ loves you. Yes, YOU! Regardless of your past, your failures, or how far you have wandered from God, His mercy is still available to you. But consider this: What if today were your last opportunity to make things right with God? Where would you spend eternity? We are living in perilous times, and tomorrow is promised to no one. The Bible warns, “Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.” (Luke 13:3) Yet God's love is so great that He sent His only begotten Son to die for our sins, that through Him we might receive everlasting life (John 3:16). Don't gamble with your eternity. Come to Jesus Christ while there is still time! If you are ready to repent of your sins and surrender your life to Jesus Christ, you can begin by sincerely praying: Heavenly Father, I confess that I am a sinner in need of Your mercy and forgiveness. I believe that Jesus Christ, Your Son, died for my sins and rose again. I turn away from my sinful ways and ask You to cleanse my heart. Lord Jesus, I surrender my life to You. Be my Savior and Lord. Help me to walk in obedience to Your Word and live a life that honors You. In Jesus' precious name, Amen. Remember, it is not merely repeating a prayer that saves you, but genuine repentance and faith in Jesus Christ. “For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.” — Romans 10:13 (KJV). If you have sincerely placed your faith in Jesus Christ, begin reading His Word and find a Bible-believing, God-fearing church where you can grow in your walk with Him. God loves you, but He will not force you to come to Him. The invitation is before you. What will you do with Jesus Christ? God bless you! 🙏🏽
